sub: Named after infaṭarat, the sky “breaking apart”, in ayah 1
theme: When the sky splits and graves open, every soul sees its deeds. So what has made man careless of his generous Lord? Angels record everything, and on the Day of Recompense only Allah’s command counts.
story: Revealed in Makkah, close in time and subject to At-Takwīr. The Prophet ﷺ named it with At-Takwīr and Al-Inshiqāq as the surahs that show the Day of Judgement as if you were seeing it.
When Muʿādh led a very long night prayer, the Prophet ﷺ asked him why he did not recite surahs like Al-Aʿlā, Aḍ-Ḍuḥā and this one instead.

Reports differ on whether ayah 6 had one man in mind: al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, Ubayy ibn Khalaf, or al-Aswad ibn Sharīq, who struck the Prophet ﷺ and was not punished at once. Its address reaches everyone who denies the Recompense.

sections.title: Sky splits, graves overturn: each soul knows what it sent and left
sections.meaning: The sky splits open, the stars scatter and fall, the seas burst into each other, and the graves are turned over. Then every soul will know what it sent ahead and what it left behind.
points: The sky splits; the stars fall and scatter
The seas burst forth into one another
Graves are overturned and the dead come out
Each soul knows what it sent ahead and left behind
sections.matters: In four short scenes the whole universe comes apart and the dead rise. It leads straight to the question that matters: what have you sent ahead, and what have you left behind?
sections.story: No specific incident. It mirrors the opening of At-Takwīr, which ends with the same idea: a soul will know what it has brought.
explained: Infaṭarat: the sky cracks open. The stars, its beauty, fall and scatter. The seas are fujjirat: burst open into one another until fresh and salt water become one sea. The graves are buʿthirat: their soil is turned over and the dead are brought out alive.
At that moment every soul knows mā qaddamat wa akhkharat. Either the deeds it did and the duties it left undone, or the deeds it did itself and the good or bad customs it left for others to follow.
teaches: The world you know has an end.
What you neglect is written, not just what you do.
A good custom you start keeps earning for you after death.
A bad custom you start keeps adding to your account.
sections.hook: Four idhā lines (1–4), each ending in -at, then the answer in 5. Both this surah and At-Takwīr answer their “when” lines with ʿalimat nafs, “a soul will know”.

sections.title: Fooled about his Generous Creator, man denies Recompense while angels record
sections.meaning: O man, what has fooled you about your generous Lord, who created you, shaped you perfectly, balanced you, and put you together in whatever form He willed? No! The real problem is that you deny the Recompense, while noble angels record everything you do.
points: O man, what deceived you about your Generous Lord?
He created, shaped, balanced and assembled you as He willed
Noble guardian angels write down all you do
sections.matters: It names the real trap: mistaking Allah’s generosity and patience for permission to disobey. His kindness in creating you should lead to thanks, not carelessness, especially when every deed is being written.
sections.story: Reports differ on whether ayah 6 had one particular disbeliever in mind. Several names are given, but the question is put to every person who grows careless about his Lord.
explained: Mā gharraka: what fooled you? This is a warning, not a question inviting an excuse. Allah is al-Karīm, the Generous, who does not punish at once. Man takes that patience as safety and keeps sinning, when it should make him grateful.

He created you, then sawwāka, made you whole, then ʿadalaka, balanced your body and limbs, and put you together in whatever form He willed, even resembling a parent or relative. Kallā: the real cause is that you deny ad-dīn, the Recompense. Yet noble angels are writing down everything you do.
teaches: Don’t let Allah’s patience make you careless.
Your balanced body is a gift that calls for thanks.
Denying accountability is the root of disobedience.
Live knowing that noble angels are writing it all down.
sections.hook: Allah is al-Karīm (6) and the recording angels are kirām (11): the same root. Ayah 7 has three verbs in a row ending in -ka: khalaqaka, fa-sawwāka, fa-ʿadalaka.

sections.title: Righteous in bliss, wicked in Fire; that Day no soul helps another
sections.meaning: The righteous will be in bliss and the wicked in Hellfire, burning in it on the Day of Recompense and never leaving it. What will make you understand that Day? It is the Day no soul can do anything for another, and the command belongs to Allah alone.
points: The righteous in bliss, the wicked in Hellfire
They burn in it on that Day and never leave
What will make you know the Day of Recompense?
No soul can help another; the command is Allah’s
sections.matters: The surah ends by answering its own warning. Those who deny the Recompense are shown the two final homes and a Day when no friend, relative or power can help, because the judgement is Allah’s alone.
sections.story: No specific incident. It completes the warning to those who deny the Day of Recompense.
explained: Al-abrār, who fulfilled the rights of Allah and of people, are in naʿīm, bliss of heart, soul and body. Al-fujjār, whose hearts and deeds went bad, are in jaḥīm. They enter and burn in it on Yawm ad-Dīn and are never absent from it, not even for an hour.

The question is asked twice to show how immense that Day is: what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is? Then the answer: no soul can do anything for another, not even for someone dear. Al-amru yawmaʾidhin lillāh: that Day, the command is Allah’s alone.
teaches: Fulfilling the rights of Allah and people leads to bliss.
Don’t rely on anyone but Allah to save you on that Day.
The punishment of those who deny is never lightened.
All judgement belongs to Allah, now and then.
sections.hook: Ayat 13 and 14 mirror each other: inna al-abrāra la-fī naʿīm / wa inna al-fujjāra la-fī jaḥīm. Yawm ad-dīn comes three times (15, 17, 18), after ad-dīn in ayah 9.

groups.text: The sky splits apart, and the stars fall and scatter.
Seas burst forth and graves are overturned. Then each soul knows what it sent ahead and left behind.
O man, what fooled you about your Generous Lord, who created, shaped and formed you as He willed?
No! You deny the Recompense, yet noble angels are writing down everything you do.
The righteous are in bliss; the wicked burn in Hellfire on that Day and never leave it.
What is the Day of Recompense? A Day no soul can help another, and the command is Allah’s.

1.explain: Infaṭarat: the sky cracks and splits open.

2.explain: Al-kawākib intatharat: the stars fall and scatter, and the sky loses its beauty.

3.explain: Fujjirat: the seas burst open into one another, fresh and salt water mixing into one sea, or they overflow.

4.explain: Buʿthirat: graves are turned upside down, their soil overturned, and the dead inside are brought out alive.

5.explain: Mā qaddamat wa akhkharat: what it sent ahead and held back. Either deeds done and duties left undone, or its own deeds and the good or bad customs it left behind.

6.explain: Mā gharraka: what fooled you about al-Karīm, your Generous Lord, until you disobeyed Him? His generosity in not punishing at once is no reason to be careless.
6.why: Reports name different men: al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, Ubayy ibn Khalaf, Abū al-Ashadd ibn Kaladah, or al-Aswad ibn Sharīq, who struck the Prophet ﷺ and was not punished right away.

7.explain: Khalaqaka: He created you from nothing. Fa-sawwāka: made you whole with sound limbs. Fa-ʿadalaka: balanced you, one hand or foot no longer than the other.

8.explain: Fī ayyi ṣūratin mā shāʾa rakkabak: He put you together in whatever form He willed, such as resembling a father, mother or uncle.

9.explain: Kallā: His generosity is no excuse. Bal tukadhdhibūna bid-dīn: the real reason is that you deny the Recompense and the Reckoning.

10.explain: Ḥāfiẓīn: angels appointed over you, keeping watch and recording your deeds.

11.explain: Kirāman kātibīn: noble in Allah’s sight, writing down your words and actions. So don’t meet them with evil deeds.

12.explain: Yaʿlamūna mā tafʿalūn: they know everything you do, good or bad, including actions of the heart.

13.explain: Al-abrār: those who fulfilled the rights of Allah and of His servants. They are in naʿīm, bliss.

14.explain: Al-fujjār: those who fell short of those rights, whose hearts went bad and so their deeds did too. They are in jaḥīm, the blazing Fire.

15.explain: Yaṣlawnahā: they enter it and suffer its heat on Yawm ad-Dīn, the Day of Recompense.

16.explain: Wa mā hum ʿanhā bi-ghāʾibīn: they will never be absent from it, not for an hour, with no lightening and no death.

17.explain: Wa mā adrāka: what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is? The question shows how immense it is.

18.explain: Thumma mā adrāka: the same question again, to make that Day feel even greater.

19.explain: No soul can benefit another, except as Allah permits. Al-amru yawmaʾidhin lillāh: the command is Allah’s alone, and no one will dispute it.
